land.text: the State of Guatemala within the Federal Republic of Central America, without Los Altos (separate from 1838)

predecessors.note: Page: 'Declared from the Federal Republic of Central America: 17 April 1839'; 'From 1823 to 1841, it was part of the Federal Republic of Central America.'

capitals.name: Guatemala City
capitals.note: Infobox capital. The page dates the new city to 1776 ('officially founded in 1776, became known as La Nueva Guatemala de la Asunción'), after the Santa Marta earthquakes of 1773 destroyed Antigua.

correction.text: the State of Guatemala from 17 April 1839, without Los Altos

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1840 but the page makes the State of Guatemala independent of the Federal Republic on 17 April 1839. Los Altos had proclaimed its independence on 2 February 1838 (Los Altos page), so the 1840 outline without Los Altos is the 1839 state.

correction.text: Guatemala with Los Altos forcibly reincorporated (infobox 'January 1840'), including the Soconusco declared 'part of the Quetzaltenango District in 1840'

keyframe_review.note: 82,732 km2 for 1840-1841: Guatemala without Los Altos. The Los Altos page: 'Forcible reincorporation into Guatemala: January 1840' (the body says Carrera 'forcibly annexed Quetzaltenango and much of Los Altos back into conservative Guatemala' on 2 April 1840), so by 1840 the western highlands (103 cells, 26,000 km2) and the Soconusco (30 cells of Chiapas in Cliopatria's Los Altos row) belong to Guatemala, not to a separate Los Altos; Cliopatria keeps its Los Altos row to 1841 and adds the highlands to Guatemala only in 1842. The Soconusco leaves in 1842 (ledger).

109,084 km2 for 1842-1912 against the infobox 108,889 km2 (undated; ratio 1.00): the modern outline, with Los Altos included. The Soconusco is outside it from the Mexican occupation of 1842. The shape holds through 1848-1849, when Los Altos was independent again from 26 August 1848 to 8 May 1849 (ledger). It draws six border cells of Belize (Toledo, Cayo, Orange Walk), the edge of the claim, not the 12,272 km2 Guatemala claims from the Sibun to the Sarstoon; the pages give no 19th-century frontier with Mexico, Honduras or El Salvador, so the outline is the modern one (unverified: page budget).
109,196 km2 for 1913-1919: one cell differs from the 1842 outline (Petén to Chiapas, 112 km2): rasterisation noise, no event on the page. Infobox ratio 1.00.
109,084 km2 for 1920-1978, the 1842 outline; infobox ratio 1.00. The page gives no border change in these years.

108,915 km2 for 1979-1991: one cell on the El Salvador border differs from the 1842 outline (about 170 km2): rasterisation noise. Belize became independent on 21 September 1981 and Guatemala recognised it only in 1991 (Belize dispute page), so no Guatemalan loss is drawn.

109,084 km2 for 1992-2023, the 1842 outline. The Belize page: the claim 'amounts to 12,272 km2 ... or roughly 53% of Belizean territory' and went to the ICJ after the referendums of 15 April 2018 (Guatemala) and 8 May 2019 (Belize); the shape does not draw it.

region.text: the State of Guatemala without Los Altos

ledger.note: 1839: Guatemala becomes independent of the Federal Republic. 'Declared from the Federal Republic of Central America: 17 April 1839'; 'prior to that [21 March 1847] it was the State of Guatemala (Estado de Guatemala) from 17 April 1839.' Los Altos had been a breakaway state since 1838.

region.text: Los Altos as Cliopatria draws it in 1840: the eight departments of western Guatemala plus the Soconusco, which the Los Altos page says the state included

ledger.note: 1840: Carrera reincorporates Los Altos. Infobox 'Forcible reincorporation into Guatemala: January 1840'; the body has Carrera 'forcibly annexed Quetzaltenango and much of Los Altos back into conservative Guatemala' on 2 April 1840 and the captured leaders paraded on 17 February 1840. Cliopatria carries Los Altos as a separate row to 1841.

region.text: the Soconusco, in the southwest corner of Chiapas

ledger.note: 1842: Mexico takes the Soconusco. Guatemala had declared it 'part of the Quetzaltenango District in 1840'; in 1842 'Santa Anna sent troops to press the population to formally unite with Mexico, and Soconusco did so' (no month). The 1882 treaty later 'split the Soconusco region, with the greater part going to Mexico'; Cliopatria draws the 1882 line from 1842.

1847: the Republic of Guatemala. 'On 21 March 1847, Guatemala declared itself an independent republic and Carrera became its first president'; the official name 'Republic of Guatemala' dates from the decree of that day.

region.text: Los Altos without its Soconusco: the eight departments of western Guatemala (Totonicapán, Huehuetenango, Quetzaltenango, San Marcos, Retalhuleu, Suchitepéquez, Sololá, Quiché)

ledger.note: 1848: Los Altos secedes again. Quetzaltenango's capitulars 'declared that Los Altos was an independent state once again on 26 August 1848.' The page does not say which of the eight departments followed it; the whole of the old state is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Los Altos without its Soconusco: the eight departments of western Guatemala (Totonicapán, Huehuetenango, Quetzaltenango, San Marcos, Retalhuleu, Suchitepéquez, Sololá, Quiché)

ledger.note: 1849: Carrera ends Los Altos for good. 'The existence of Los Altos lasted until 8 May 1849'; Carrera 'took Quetzaltenango and remained in the plaza' and 'triumphantly entered Guatemala City on 8 August 1849.'

wars.name: Carrera's reconquest of Los Altos

zones.text: Los Altos without its Soconusco: the eight departments of western Guatemala (Totonicapán, Huehuetenango, Quetzaltenango, San Marcos, Retalhuleu, Suchitepéquez, Sololá, Quiché)

wars.outcome: Los Altos was forcibly reincorporated into Guatemala in January 1840 (infobox) after Carrera's campaign; the captured leaders were paraded on 17 February 1840.
wars.note: The page dates the reincorporation both 'January 1840' (infobox) and 2 April 1840 (body); the Soconusco was annexed by Mexico 'taking advantage of the chaos' (undated on that page, 1842 on the Soconusco page).

wars.name: Second Los Altos revolt

zones.text: Los Altos without its Soconusco: the eight departments of western Guatemala (Totonicapán, Huehuetenango, Quetzaltenango, San Marcos, Retalhuleu, Suchitepéquez, Sololá, Quiché)

wars.outcome: Los Altos declared independence again on 26 August 1848 and was suppressed by Carrera on 8 May 1849; Agustín Guzmán's attack on Guatemala City in October 1849 failed and he died that night.
wars.note: The page is silent on fighting between August 1848 and May 1849.

wars.name: Guatemalan-Salvadoran War of 1863
wars.outcome: The page records that Carrera's rivalry with Gerardo Barrios 'escalated into open war in 1863' and that Carrera 'besieged and occupied San Salvador' (no month); it gives no border change.
wars.note: The title is the researcher's; the page names no peace and no territory. Reviewer: the occupation of San Salvador is on the page but not yet in the ledger (gap).

wars.name: Barrios's war for Central American union
wars.outcome: Failure: Justo Rufino Barrios 'waged war in an unsuccessful attempt' to reunite Central America and died at the Battle of Chalchuapa 'in El Salvador in April 1885'; the border did not change.
wars.note: The title is the researcher's; the page gives no day for Barrios's death. A union of states would be an association (rule 4), never territory.

wars.name: Belizean-Guatemalan territorial dispute
wars.outcome: Unsettled: Guatemala agreed to recognise British sovereignty in the Wyke-Aycinena Treaty of 1859 (signed 30 April 1859, History of Guatemala page) but later called it a cession for a road never built, and a liberal government 'declared the treaty void' (1871); Belize became independent on 21 September 1981, Guatemala recognised it in 1991, and the claim to 12,272 km2 (about 53% of Belize) went to the ICJ in 2019.
wars.note: No zone is listed because no ground was held: Guatemala 'threatened to invade' in February 1948 and pro-Guatemalan fighters crossed the border on 21 January 1958; the claimed land (from the Sibun to the Sarstoon, all of Toledo and Stann Creek Districts) is Belizean on Cliopatria's rows.

certainty.note: The Soconusco was claimed by both Guatemala and Mexico until the 1882 treaty, and no page opened gives a boundary survey with Honduras, El Salvador or British Honduras.

The Mexican frontier is the 1882 treaty line ('set the modern border'). The Belize frontier is the exception: disputed since 1859 and before the ICJ since 2019 (soft). The Honduran and Salvadoran frontiers are not described on any page opened here.

notes: Cliopatria's seven shapes are all the modern outline (420 cells) except 1840-1841 (317 cells, without Los Altos); 1913 and 1979 differ by one cell. Not settled: (1) Los Altos: the page gives both 2 February and 2 April 1838 for its founding and January and 2 April 1840 for its end; the los-altos dossier (another group) and Cliopatria's Los Altos row (1840-1841, 35,593 km2, which includes 30 cells of Chiapas) should be set against this dossier's 1840 reincorporation. (2) The Soconusco in 1840-1842: only the Soconusco page's wording; the 1882 treaty's lesser share that stayed Guatemalan is not described and no gain is recorded. (3) The History of Guatemala page (opened for borders) has no 1882 Mexican treaty, no 1933 Honduras arbitration and no 1981 Belize entry; the Mexican boundary appears there only as a dispute Barrios took to US mediation in 1880. The Honduran and Salvadoran frontiers are the modern lines on no page (page budget: five pages). (4) The Guatemalan claim to Belize is not drawn: it is recorded as a dispute, not a contest, because no ground was held. (5) The Federation of Central America of 1921-1922 is mentioned on the Guatemala page without territory (an association, not drawn). (6) The History of Guatemala page gives Los Altos' founding as 2 April 1838 (the Los Altos page 2 February), and has the Federal Republic gaining 'full independence' on its dissolution 'in 1841' against 17 April 1839 on the Guatemala page; the start date follows the Guatemala page. Names the gazetteer lacks: 'Soconusco'.
